output:
The family tools now publish one flat object, and both verification commands pass. The changed paths are all in `owns_paths`:

- `src/rooms/tools/server/tool-families.ts`: `mountFamily` publishes `action` (an enum) plus every member field, optional, merged by name. Each field's description lists the actions that take it and where it is required. A superRefine runs each action's checks at parse time: missing required arguments are named with their types, another action's arguments are refused and name their owner, and the old tool's own schema still validates the value. `execute` hands the old handler exactly what its schema parses. Family instructions gain a generated `Required: …` line per action.
- `src/rooms/tools/server/tools.ts`: `lane_pilot_browser_qa` instructions now say where `runId` comes from (the dispatch and wait receipts carry the `lprun_…` id) and what `envClass` means.
- `tests/pm-tool-families.test.ts`: new assertions for the flat schema, the generated required lines, the browser_qa instruction text, the browser_qa refusal, foreign-argument messages, and a list sent as JSON text. The instruction-length check now asserts the 4000 cap the code enforces.

Results:
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` exits 0.
- `npx vitest run tests/pm-tool-families.test.ts tests/pm-tool-mentions.test.ts`: 15 of 15 pass.
- Also ran `tool-presentation`, `native-agent-overlay`, `stages/browser-qa`, `qa-host` and `guard-route-first`: 28 of 28 pass. I did not run the full suite; that is for the coordinator.
- The helpers family instructions come to 3902 characters, under the 4000 cap, so the full variant is used.

Things to know:
- A value of the wrong type fails at the shared flat field as `cases: Invalid input` and does not name the action. Missing and foreign arguments do name it. I left this because the field types must stay published.
- `lane_pilot_schedule` (`src/rooms/schedule/server/schedule-tools.ts`) still uses a top-level `discriminatedUnion`, so the bridge probably shows it as bare `{type: object}` too. It is outside `owns_paths` and not a family, so I left it alone; it needs its own task.
- No project rule was set aside. I did not use the GitNexus tools because the repo has no `.gitnexus/` index.

dispatchContext.memoryText:
- Full plugin backups use a versioned JSON payload (`kind: 'bb-project-folders-backup'`, version 1) containing settings and all 11 durable tables: folders, folder_paths, thread_places, folder_rules, project_rules, project_order, execution_defaults, session_policies, preferences, item_styles, and folder_archives. Imports preserve row IDs and run in one transaction; invalid backups and imports during an active move or archive are rejected. Transient tables (exports, pending_exports, project_moves, thread_moves, section_moves) are excluded. This adds no schema changes and preserves the existing appearance-only export/import flow.
- Execution defaults can pin a chat environment as `folder` or `worktree`. Resolve the pin nearest-first across section, ancestors, project, and global settings. A `worktree` pin preselects a managed worktree on the folder host in both New chat and the composer chip; spawn must preserve that managed-worktree selection. With no pin, keep the existing folder/section-provider behavior. Groups must never become chat environments.
- Errand, QA, and reviewer helper threads are read-only for repository files; specialists may write under `.agents/`. Writers retain full worktree access. Wait backstops report helper edits as `repo_edited` with changed files and do not revert them.
